meta.title: Operation of Digital Actophotometer in Pharmacology Laboratory

sections.purpose: To measure spontaneous locomotor activity of rodents by counting photocell beam interruptions to assess CNS drug effects on motor activity in pharmacological screening experiments.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacology laboratory for locomotor activity studies, sedation screening, drug abuse potential assessment, and CNS pharmacology experiments.
procedure: Switch on the digital actophotometer and confirm the display initializes to zero.
Allow the instrument to complete self-diagnostic tests.
Clean the transparent animal activity cage with 70% ethanol and allow to dry — lingering odour from prior animal markedly biases exploratory behaviour.
Acclimatize the test animal (mouse 20–25 g or rat 150–200 g) for a minimum of 30–60 minutes in the testing room before any procedure.
Administer the drug or vehicle as per protocol; note exact administration time.
Place the animal in the actophotometer chamber at the designated time post-administration.
Press the start button and begin counting.
Record the photocell interruption count at specified intervals (typically every 5 minutes for 30 minutes).
Observe and document qualitative behaviour: level of arousal, sedation, ataxia, stereotypy, Straub tail response.
After the session, remove the animal promptly; return to housing cage.
Decontaminate the chamber with 70% ethanol between all animals.
Calculate the mean ± SEM counts for each group; compare drug groups vs. control using appropriate statistics.
Document all data in the experimental protocol sheet.
precautions: Perform experiments in a low-noise, stable light environment — ambient noise and light fluctuations distort photocell readings.
Use the same time of day for all experiments to control for circadian rhythm variation in activity.
Animals must be food and water satiated before testing unless fasting is part of the protocol.
Follow CPCSEA guidelines for use and care of laboratory animals.
Acclimatize animals properly — stressed or naïve animals show elevated baseline activity that masks drug effects.
Disinfect cages between animals — odour from previous animals elicits defensive behaviour that elevates counts.
Record the room temperature (ideally 22–24°C) at each experiment — activity varies significantly with temperature.
